ordered_diagnoses: Congenital heart disease with shunt reversal

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic exertional chest pain and shortness of breath with progressive cyanosis and lower extremity edema
salient_findings: Recurrent post-activity chest pain and shortness of breath for more than 11 years
Bilateral lower extremity edema for one week
Cyanosis developed after an episode of severe cough and hemoptysis in 2016
key_facts: Patient is a 39-year-old male
Symptoms began in 2010 with post-activity chest pain and shortness of breath
Patient was initially acyanotic from 2010 to 2016
Cyanosis developed after an episode of severe cough and hemoptysis in 2016
Femoral artery oxygen saturation was measured at 88.5%
Plasma N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide was 94.2 pg/ml in August 2021
Chest CT showed enlarged hilar shadow and widened pulmonary arteries
Echocardiography showed markedly enlarged right atrium and right ventricle with tricuspid regurgitation
Estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure was 55 mmHg in 2021
Right Heart Catheterization showed pulmonary artery pressure was 60/39 mmHg
Transesophageal Echocardiography revealed a patent foramen ovale with a continuous, pure right-to-left shunt

raw.champion: Congenital heart disease with shunt reversal
raw.rationale: The patient's history of initial acyanosis followed by development of cyanosis after a severe respiratory episode, combined with the presence of a patent foramen ovale and a continuous right-to-left shunt, supports the diagnosis of a congenital heart disease with shunt reversal, which is consistent with the patient's long-standing symptoms and echocardiography findings.

rejected.label: Eisenmenger syndrome
rejected.why: While Eisenmenger syndrome involves a congenital heart defect with shunt reversal, the patient's specific defect is a patent foramen ovale, which is not explicitly mentioned as a typical cause of Eisenmenger syndrome.

rejected.label: Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension
rejected.why: The patient's pulmonary hypertension is likely secondary to the congenital heart disease rather than idiopathic, given the presence of a patent foramen ovale and shunt reversal.

rejected.label: Cor pulmonale
rejected.why: Cor pulmonale refers to right-sided heart failure due to pulmonary disease, but the patient's primary issue is a congenital heart defect with shunt reversal, not a pulmonary disease.

rejected.label: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
rejected.why: Pulmonary angiography showed no evidence of pulmonary embolism or pulmonary arteriovenous fistulae, making this diagnosis unlikely.
